paper_metadata.title: One novel Mg-Y-Ni dilute alloy with an excellent combination of strong high-temperature strength and fast dissolution rate

evidence.quote: this work provides one novel Mg-0.76Y-0.79Ni dilute alloy using common extrusion method. Two alloys Mg-1.97Y-0.22Ni and Mg-5.53Y are also studied as the comparisons.
The three alloys used in this study included Mg-0.76Y-0.79Ni, Mg-1.97Y-0.22Ni, and Mg-5.53Y, in weight percents (wt%).

These alloys were prepared by mixing high-purity Mg and master alloys including Mg-30wt%Y and Mg-5wt%Ni, melting in resistance furnaces at 1053 K, and casting followed by air cooling. The whole process was protected by an atmosphere of CO2 and SF6 with a volume ratio of 100:1
The homogenization treatment was performed at 693 K for 24 h

the extrusion was performed at 623 K with the extrusion speed at 0.5 mm·s-1 and the extrusion ratio as 9:1. ... All the extruded alloys were promptly cooled with water to preserve the instantaneous microstructures.

attributes.morphology: parallel to (0002) trace, mixed with lath-like phases

evidence.quote: Only a few <c> components are lying on the (0002) plane trace, while most of the <a> dislocations are parallel to the (0002) trace and mixed with the lath-like phases. So the inheritance of basal dislocations can be confirmed in the initial YN11 alloy
Instead of smooth fractures and deep dimples, sharp cleavages and obvious voids are found in YN20 alloy.
Due to the high solubility of RE atoms in Mg matrix and the rapid aging response of Mg-RE alloys, the solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening effects can be easily achieved
the β′ precipitates composed by Mg and Gd elements could suppress the grain boundary sliding and could strengthen the alloy significantly.
